objective: Directly observe on the target that one valid candidate run performs no read outside the supplied W*H source region and no write outside the supplied H*P output buffer, using a P > W configuration.
observation: Post-run target output buffer contents, the before and after guard canary slot values, and any target memory-fault or bounds-check report emitted during the run, including any source-region or output-region guard-page fault.
pass_condition: Accept only if (1) no memory-fault or bounds-check report is emitted for either a source-region or an output-region access; (2) the before and after guard canary slots equal their recorded baseline sentinel values (secondary confirmation); and (3) at least one output-buffer slot differs from its sentinel initialization, proving the kernel executed and wrote within the buffer. Reject on any fault/report or any changed canary. A write observed from an extra thread with xid >= W or yid >= H is not counted as a valid-invocation bound violation; the specified launch ensures no such thread exists.
setup: Build the unmodified candidate kernel. Use W=256, H=128, P=320 (P > W; W and H are positive multiples of the cited TILE_DIM=16). Launch exactly one work-item per logical coordinate: block dimension 16x16 and grid dimension W/16=16 by H/16=8, so the produced (xid,yid) set is exactly [0,256) x [0,128). If the candidate uses a different tile T or a non-CUDA work-item indexing scheme, require and record an equivalent launch that yields exactly the same [0,W) x [0,H) coordinate set, or require and verify candidate-side guards that suppress any work-item with xid >= W or yid >= H before any memory access. Place the W*H source region so that the pages immediately before and immediately after it are inaccessible (or run under a target memory-bounds checker that reports every out-of-region source access). Allocate the output buffer of exactly H*P = 40960 elements and protect the entire output region with inaccessible guard pages immediately before and immediately after the H*P region (or run under a target memory-bounds checker that reports every out-of-region output access). Sentinel canary slots immediately adjacent to the buffer may be recorded only as secondary confirmation, not as the primary detection mechanism. Initialize every output slot and every canary slot to a distinct sentinel, fill the source with unique binary32 values none equal to the sentinel, set shiftX=5 and shiftY=7, run one valid invocation, synchronize, and read back the buffer and canaries.
